description: This collection provides synthetic electric-vehicle charging events generated from 185 days of observations at a Caltech charging site in the United States. University of Alberta researchers use conditional tabular generative adversarial networks and kernel density estimation to produce 29,600 synthetic days for machine-learning experiments. Each row supplies connection time on a zero-to-twenty-four-hour scale, charging duration in hours, delivered energy in kilowatt-hours and a day identifier. Mendeley version 2 publishes one CSV free under CC BY 4.0. The expanded horizon is simulated and does not represent eighty years of observed charging or nationally representative travel behaviour. Correlations and capacity constraints inherited from the generator limit transfer to other parking sites. A reviewer-assessed use is training charging-control agents or stress-testing coordinated demand rules. model-pypsa and model-sumo are related electricity and transport simulation tools, without verified direct interfaces. No CSV, statistical comparison or learning algorithm was executed.
